title: ARIA roles must sit inside their required parents
summary: An element has an ARIA role that must be inside a particular parent role, such as listitem inside list, and is not. Add the parent or use native HTML.
problem: An element has a role that must be contained by a particular parent role. For example, role="listitem" belongs inside role="list". When the parent is missing, the item does not belong to any structure.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users depend on the parent to hear context such as list size and position. Without the parent the child can be announced with no context, or ignored.
steps: Find the child element and its role in the scan result.
Check in the WAI-ARIA specification which parent role it needs.
Wrap the elements in a parent with that role, as direct ancestors with no other roles in between.
Better still, use native HTML such as <ul> and <li>, which gives the correct structure without ARIA.
whyItMatters: Items without their parent are announced out of context. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Re-run the scan, and check the elements in your browser's accessibility tree. Each should appear under its parent role.
